impact_summary: Amazon DynamoDB in the us-east-1 Region experienced increased API error rates from 11:48 PM Oct 19 to 2:40 AM Oct 20 (PDT) after the regional DNS record was left empty, and global table replicas in us-east-1 saw prolonged replication lag until 2:32 AM. Subsequent impairment of EC2 instance launches (2:25 AM to 1:50 PM Oct 20) and Network Load Balancer connection errors (5:30 AM to 2:09 PM Oct 20) extended the disruption, and dependent services including Lambda, ECS/EKS/Fargate, Redshift, STS, Amazon Connect, the AWS Management Console and the Support Center experienced errors for periods ranging from roughly two hours to over a day, with some Redshift clusters affected until 4:05 AM Oct 21.

action_items.action: Modify the DNS Enactor so every Route53 transaction verifies that the plan being written is newer than the currently applied plan, not only a one-time check before application begins.
Change the plan clean-up process so it never deletes the currently active plan or any plan that a live endpoint depends on, regardless of generation age.
Add automated detection and self-repair for the empty-DNS-record inconsistent state so the system recovers without manual operator intervention.
Add alarms on regional DynamoDB endpoint record count and on Enactor apply latency or retry counts, alerting on-call before DNS records become empty.
Reduce the EC2 DWFM dependency on DynamoDB so lease state checks can continue or degrade gracefully during DynamoDB endpoint failures.
Develop and rehearse a documented, staged recovery runbook for DWFM lease re-establishment at full fleet scale, including throttling and selective host restart procedures.
Gate health check subsystem admission of newly launched EC2 instances on confirmed network state propagation before they are added to NLB service.
Add safeguards so health check degradation cannot trigger automatic AZ DNS failover that removes large amounts of capacity, with a manual override that is tested in advance.
Remove the cross-region dependency of Redshift IAM user-group resolution on an IAM API in us-east-1 by making it regionally local or cached.
Audit critical services for hard dependencies on us-east-1 control-plane components (including EC2 launches and DynamoDB) and define cell-based or static-stability fallbacks for them.
Add testing of failover paths, including the account metadata subsystem used by the Support Center, to verify that cross-region failover returns valid responses.
Add a Lambda throttling and scaling safeguard so that loss of capacity in the underlying compute layer does not leave internal systems under-scaled after health check failures.
Ensure Lambda's SQS-polling internal subsystem automatically recovers after dependency failures instead of requiring manual restoration.
